headline: Geopolitical Fog Over Hormuz Sets a Cautious Tone for Monday's Open
body_html:
Wall Street prepares to reopen Monday with geopolitical risk front and center after a weekend dominated by Middle East tensions. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed measurably following a series of attacks, and stalled U.S.-Iran nuclear talks are keeping crude prices elevated — a dynamic already rippling through Asian equity markets, where shares traded cautiously overnight, and into Indian bourses, which fell sharply on sustained oil-price pressure.

Friday's session offered a mixed but instructive backdrop. Breadth in our universe was modestly negative — 259 names advanced against 286 decliners across 549 names tracked — yet sector dispersion told a sharper story. Energy and Materials led with gains of 1.35% and 1.21%, respectively, while Semiconductors added 1.13%. Software lagged badly, off 1.38%, dragged by broad selling across IT-services and cybersecurity names. Homebuilders slipped 0.60% as rate and sentiment concerns lingered.

At the open, traders will be watching oil-linked equities for follow-through, given that Gulf markets managed modest gains overnight even amid Hormuz disruption. Diplomatic noise around the Gaza conflict and the latest U.S.–South Korea defense posture headlines could weigh on risk appetite. The semiconductor tape — notably strong on Friday — bears close monitoring for signs of sustained rotation or a simple one-day relief bid.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Shipping Slowdown Keeps Energy Bulls in the Driver's Seat
briefs.body: Vessel-tracking data confirmed a measurable decline in tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz following recent attacks, lending support to crude prices heading into the week. Energy was the top-performing sector in Friday's session with a 1.35% advance, and the supply-disruption narrative shows little sign of easing as U.S.-Iran talks remain deadlocked.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Buck Broader Weakness; MaxLinear and AMD Lead Friday Charge
briefs.body: The Semiconductor sector posted a 1.13% gain on Friday, defying a negative breadth reading across the broader universe. MaxLinear surged 10.68% to top the leaderboard, while AMD added 6.50% and memory-chip name Sandisk climbed 7.39%, suggesting selective demand for chip exposure even as Software names retreated sharply.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Suffers Worst Sectoral Loss as N-able, ZoomInfo Slide
briefs.body: Software ended Friday as the clear laggard, dropping 1.38% at the sector level. N-able fell 6.52% and ZoomInfo shed 6.03%, while Qualys declined 5.02%, reflecting continued pressure on recurring-revenue technology businesses. Investors appear to be rotating away from premium-multiple software names amid an uncertain macro backdrop.

briefs.headline: Kushner Diplomatic Overture Follows Rare Contact With Hamas
briefs.body: Senior U.S. envoy Jared Kushner is set to hold direct discussions with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu after a rare back-channel engagement with Hamas representatives, according to weekend reports. The initiative comes as Israeli strikes continued in Gaza, keeping Middle East diplomatic channels unusually active and adding to the geopolitical variables weighing on markets at the open.

briefs.headline: Trump Administration Eyes Expanded Economic Pressure on Tehran
briefs.body: The White House is actively exploring additional levers to tighten economic pressure on Iran as negotiations over its nuclear program stall, according to reporting over the weekend. The discussion coincides with Iran's parliament advancing legislation aimed at curtailing foreign influence, signaling a hardening of positions on both sides that could prolong the oil-market uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Pentagon Directed to Scale Back Military Drills With South Korea
briefs.body: President Trump has instructed the Defense Department to reduce the scope of joint military exercises conducted with South Korea, a move that introduces fresh uncertainty into U.S. alliance posture in the Pacific. The directive adds to a weekend of geopolitically charged headlines that traders will need to price alongside an already tense Middle East environment at Monday's open.
